abstract: Mononuclear bis(carbyne) complexes featuring two multiply bonded carbyne ligands at a single metal center, are an exceptionally rare class of organometallic compounds. Despite considerable advances in multiple bonding involving heavier group 14 elements, the synthesis of their heavier congeners, bis(tetrylidyne) complexes [L n M(ER) 2 ] (E = Si–Pb), remains extremely challenging owing to the lack of suitable synthetic strategies.

title: Stereochemical and electronic complementarity drives both arene and facial selectivity for carbohydrate CH–π Interactions
abstract: CH-π interactions between a sugar and an aromatic amino acid play an important role in carbohydrate recognition by proteins. Glycoconjugate model systems have been instructive in highlighting the importance of electronic and dispersive effects in driving carbohydrate-arene association in aqueous solution. These interactions have been probed using NMR, leveraging ring current-induced magnetic fields in arenes to effect chemical shift perturbations (CSPs) in select glycoside proton resonances upon association with aromatic rings.

title: Beyond Candidate Generation: A Validation-First Protocol for AI-Assisted Transition-State Discovery
abstract: Machine-learned models can now propose three-dimensional transition-state (TS) geometries in seconds, but a candidate geometry is not a validated TS. The gap between a plausible structure and a mechanistically meaningful barrier—one imaginary frequency, the intended atom pair, the correct connectivity, and a consistent electronic state—remains the bottleneck in AI-assisted computational chemistry. We present a validation-first protocol that separates candidate generation from physical validation.

title: Autonomous Experimentation Enables Rapid Optimization of Photochemical Continuous-Flow Synthesis of Diazaxanthilidene Fluorophores
abstract: Photoconvertible diazaxanthilidene dyes enable optical labeling and tracking in live cells, but the batch photocyclization that generates them requires days of irradiation and analog-specific optimization. Here we report a closed-loop continuous-flow platform that uses Bayesian optimization to tune light intensity, temperature, flow rate, and concentration. In campaigns on the parent diazaxanthilidene and four analogs, the platform improved throughput for four of five compounds.

title: Sustainable and Scalable Electrochemical Decarboxylative Cyanation of an Amino Acid Using KCN as Both Cyanide Source and Base
abstract: Organic nitriles are an important class of compounds found in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, as well as useful intermediates in synthesis. Decarboxylative cyanation as a method to generate nitriles enables the use of widely available carboxylic acids as starting materials. Although this method has been well-explored synthetically, current methodologies often feature poor atom economy or require harsh reaction conditions. Herein, an electrochemical method for the decarboxylative cyanation of Cbz-protected alanine that uses inexpensive KCN as the cyanide source has been developed.

title: Small-data pH-resolved kernel modelling of flotation collectors
abstract: Small, heterogeneous datasets are common in chemometrics, yet their predictive ceiling is rarely quantified. We assembled 19 flotation collectors from 15 literature sources (116 pH-resolved recovery points) and asked how much of the label, curve maximum and full pH curve can be predicted from molecular descriptors. The model combines DFT, Mordred and local descriptors in an additive molecule/pH kernel with a target branch for the label and maximum and a shape branch for the normalized curve.

title: HRnSiH3: A Radon Hydride with Near-Zero Dissociation Energy, Benchmarked Against HRnF
abstract: HRnSiH3 is a genuine minimum on the PBE0/ZORA potential energy surface, but at coupled-cluster level it is not meaningfully bound against loss of its atoms. We optimised the C3v structure (H–Rn 2.008 Å, Rn–Si 2.876 Å; all harmonic frequencies real) and computed dissociation energies with a CCSD(T)/def2-TZVP plus MP2(QZ–TZ) composite, using a 60-electron effective core potential on Rn, with counterpoise and zero-point corrections. For HRnSiH3 → Rn + H + SiH3 the result is +1 kcal/mol, with an es mated uncertainty of ±3 kcal/mol, so the molecule is thermoneutral against radical fragmentation.

title: Method for Measuring Solid-State Diffusivity: Part 1. Theoretical Introduction
abstract: The reliable determination of solid-state lithium diffusivity is essential for parameterizing physics-based lithium-ion battery models. However, conventional methods misattribute electrolyte concentration polarization to solid-state diffusion, introducing systematic errors in the inferred diffusivity. This study introduces a resistance-decomposition method that explicitly accounts for electronic conduction, electrolyte transport, charge transfer, and solid-state diffusion within the Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) framework.

title: Reactive dye adsorption and recovery using a PVA/TiO2 film containing Saccharum spontaneum flower-fibre cellulose: kinetic model discrimination beyond pseudo-second-order
abstract: Reactive dyes are difficult to remove from textile effluent, and adsorbents made from discarded plant fibres offer a low-cost option. Cellulose microcrystals were isolated from the flower fibre ofSaccharum spontaneum (catkin) and incorporated with TiO2 nanoparticles into a citric acid-crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol) film prepared by solution casting. The film was characterized by FTIR, XRD, particle size analysis, FE-SEM with EDX, DSC, swelling, tensile and color measurements.

title: Nucleotides trigger the spontaneous emergence of hierarchical nanolamellar architectures in coacervate-like polyelectrolyte multilayers
abstract: Spontaneous generation of hierarchical order over multiple length scales remains a major challenge in soft materials because it typically relies on external patterning or multistep fabrication strategies. Here we show that a coacervate-like, exponentially growing poly(L-lysine)/hyaluronic acid (PLL/HA) multilayer autonomously reorganizes into a hierarchical architecture following simple exposure to ATP under aqueous conditions. Within minutes, the initially homogeneous film evolves into a sponge-like network of micrometer-sized cavities separated by thin walls containing PLL, HA and ATP.

title: Post-Polymerization Editing of Polymer Tacticity
abstract: The tacticity of polymers impacts their macroscopic properties. Methods to precisely 10 control polymer tacticity prior to or during polymerization are well known; however, postpolymerization editing of tacticity remains underexplored. Here, we report a strategy for visible light-driven polymer tacticity editing through continuous C–H exchange at stereogenic sites along the polymer backbone. This approach can transform isotactic polymers into a library of products with varying tacticities and can provide access to stereoenriched polymers from atactic starting 15 materials.

title: Phase-Controlled Synthesis and Low Thermal Conductivity in Cu 4 TiTe 4
abstract: The synthesis of phase-pure Cu-based multinary tellurides remains challenging due to the competitive formation of stable Cu–Te binary phases, which frequently intercept the reaction pathway as secondary products. In the Cu 4 TiTe 4 system, rapid synthesis temperature mapping reveals the synthesis window, whereas precise compositional control suppresses secondary Cu–Te binaries to unlock non-equilibrium phase selection.

title: PLANTMETBENCH: A MULTIMODAL KNOWLEDGE GRAPH BENCHMARK FOR BIOSYNTHESIS PREDICTION
abstract: Plant metabolism produces a vast diversity of molecules, yet identifying the enzymes that catalyse biosynthetic reactions remains a major open problem. Existing benchmarks typically reduce this problem to isolated enzyme–reaction pairs, overlooking pathway and metabolite context that determines biological plausibility, leaving no standardised way to evaluate approaches that exploit this richer multimodal and relational structure. We present PlantMetBench, a multimodal graph benchmark built on PlantMetWiki, a curated knowledge graph of plant metabolism spanning 424 organisms.

title: Spectro-Electrochemical Decoding of Metals, Alloys, and Buried Interfaces
abstract: Metal-electrolyte interfaces govern corrosion, catalysis, energy-conversion and storage technologies, yet resolving their chemical evolution under operating conditions remains challenging. Electrochemical measurements report an integrated response, while post-mortem characterization can lose the transient sequence and spatial distribution of dissolved species. Here, we introduce the In-Situ Corrosion Monitoring Technique (ICMT), an operando spectro-electrochemical platform that converts interfacial metal dissolution into spatially and temporally resolved optical concentration fields.

title: A Refined cDICE Platform for the Controlled Production of Lipid Giant Unilamellar Vesicles
abstract: Continuous Droplet Interface Crossing Encapsulation (cDICE) is well known to be an effective alternative to the manual reverse emulsion method to produce giant unilamellar vesicles (GUV). It provides high encapsulation efficiency and enhanced user control over process variables, comparable to that offered by microfluidic approaches, without involving extensive infrastructure requirements such as clean rooms or lithography.

title: Sonochemical synthesis of imine- and aminal-linked porous organic polymers for efficient CO2 separation
abstract: The practical deployment of porous organic polymers (POPs) in gas separation applications remains challenging, in large part due to the limited scalability and time-consuming nature of conventional solvothermal synthesis. Herein, we report a facile and scalable sonochemical approach for the synthesis of POPs from cost-effective monomers. The resulting materials exhibit high BET surface areas of up to 664 m2/g and good CO2 separation performance for both CO2/N2 and CO2/CH4 mixtures.

title: Self-Driving Microscopy with Agents: Progress and Prospects
abstract: Agentic AI, powered by large language models, has increasingly been applied within self-driving laboratories and here we review its emerging role in self-driving microscopy. Microscopy is an unusually demanding target as each experiment is a sequence of interdependent decisions about where to measure, at what resolution, through which modality, and often on ambiguous evidence.

title: Phase transitions in multicomponent systems relevant to atmospheric new particle formation
abstract: Typically, molecular clusters containing sulfuric acid, water, ammonia, and/or amines initiate particle nucleation, followed by particle growth through condensation of highly oxidized organic molecules. The coexistence of multiple organic and inorganic components in these particles can lead to variations in morphology and phase state. In this study, optical and Raman microscopy were used to study multicomponent model aerosol particles representative of new particle formation and growth.

title: In-Situ Corrosion Monitoring via Gel-Confined Operando Spectro-Electrochemistry
abstract: Corrosion causes trillions of dollars in economic loss annually, yet real-time observation of interfacial alloy dissolution remains challenging due to rapid convective mixing, dynamic pH gradients, and post-dissolution side reactions. Here, we present in-situ corrosion monitoring technique (ICMT), a simple spectro-electrochemical approach that transforms buried interfacial corrosion into directly observable optical signals.

title: Is characterization worth the cost in data-driven catalyst discovery?
abstract: New catalysts are often discovered by trial and error, a search in which most candidates fail. Machine learning now shortens that search by predicting how untested formulations perform from composition alone. Measuring the physicochemical properties that govern performance should shorten it further, yet this expectation remains untested in a discovery campaign. We tested it on Pt-based propane dehydrogenation catalysts, evaluating discovery speed, prediction accuracy, and physical insight on the same materials.

title: Heteroanionic Tuning of Cooperative Ta Off-Centering in Quasi-One-Dimensional CsTaS3− x Cl x Semiconductors
abstract: The structural behavior of CsTaS3 was investigated alongside that of the new heteroanionic compound CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, synthesized via the reaction of Ta and S in a CsCl flux. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds are isostructural, crystallizing in the centrosymmetric hexagonal space group P63/mmc with split Ta positions along the face-sharing octahedral chain direction.

title: Unraveling the Correlation between Crystallite Orientation in Conjugated Polymer Thin Film and Charge Transport Properties
abstract: Despite great progress in tailoring the molecular structures of donor−acceptor (D−A) copolymers, the ability to precisely tailor their solid-state chain packing and establish a comprehensive structure−property relationship remains a grand challenge. Here, three diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based copolymers adjusting alkyl side chains with various lengths are developed to control their aggregation behavior in different solvents and the corresponding crystallite orientation in thin films, establishing the structure−charge -transport −property relationship and elucidating the underlying mechanism.

title: Online gas classification at the edge
abstract: Field applications in chemical sensing, from portable safety monitors to mobile robots, require models that are lightweight, fast to respond, and can be recalibrated from limited labelled data. Current gas classification pipelines assume controlled sampling cycles and offline feature extraction, and rely on computationally expensive models. With a few thousand neurons and sub-milliwatt power consumption, insects reliably classify odours in open environments. Inspired by the insect olfactory system, we present a neural network architecture that classifies raw sensor array readings using a sparse, high-dimensional binary representation. We evaluate it on random sequences of single gases and binary mixtures, introducing new samples dynamically and classifying gas identity from the transient sensor response. In this setting, the architecture out-performs a linear \gls{svm} on gas mixtures and matches an optimised non-linear \gls{svm}, while maintaining online class-level frequency estimates that distinguish familiar from novel stimuli. It relies exclusively on binary weights and Hebbian-based local learning, remaining computationally lightweight and well suited to ultra-low-power neuromorphic processors. We demonstrated the network on-chip with a hazardous gas detection experiment running on the mixed-signal neuromorphic chip TEXEL. The on-chip classifier yielded an accuracy of 74.6\% while running at 482 $\unit{\nano\joule}$ per inference and 27 \unit{\micro\watt} of static-power.

title: Embedded enzymes help plastics break down faster in the deep sea
abstract: Scientists have developed a way for certain types of compostable plastic to break down much faster in marine environments, from shallow coastal waters to the deep sea. The breakthrough comes from tiny enzymes embedded in the plastic that help degrade it from within.

title: ZnO/Ni interface-activated enhancement of spintronic terahertz emission from Ni/Pt bilayers
abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. Here, we report an interface-assisted enhancement of THz emission in ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructures. By placing ZnO underneath Ni while preserving the direct Ni/Pt contact, the THz amplitude is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. ZnO-, Ni-, and Pt-thickness-dependent measurements show that the emission remains governed by the Ni/Pt conversion process but is strongly affected by the ZnO/Ni bottom interface. Control samples with Al2O3, Cu, and Fe further exclude a simple underlayer, optical, or growth-quality origin. The enhancement is attributed to a short-range ZnO/Ni interface effect, possibly involving oxygen-related defects, interfacial electric fields, and modification of the Ni interfacial state. This work provides a semiconductor/ferromagnet interface-engineering strategy for activating weak Ni/Pt spintronic THz emitters.

title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

title: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning
abstract: Early-warning models in learning analytics can identify learners at risk of failure or withdrawal, but the resulting alerts are often only weakly connected to inspectable learning evidence. A risk score may indicate that intervention is needed without showing which traces, assessment events, or temporal patterns justify the alert. This paper introduces an incremental Learner Digital Twin for evidence-grounded early warning, implemented as a lightweight knowledge graph. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and it serves both as a feature-extraction substrate and as an explanation-grounding substrate. Predictive features are derived through graph-mediated queries, while features, attributions, alerts, evidence items, and raw records are represented as queryable graph entities. The framework is instantiated and evaluated on a public learning-analytics benchmark under a temporal protocol. The results show that graph-mediated feature extraction preserves the predictive behavior of equivalent raw-table features across model families and checkpoints. Generated alerts are materialized as evidence chains linking risk decisions to feature attributions, evidence items, and raw platform records. The study shows that early-warning prediction can be routed through a semantic and provenance-aware representation while preserving predictive performance and adding traceability, verifiability, and evidence-grounded explanation.

title: HorizON: A Multi-Horizon Deep Operator Network for Property Prediction of Organic Battery Stacks
abstract: Transition-metal-based batteries rely on critical elements such as lithium, cobalt, and nickel. Their extraction creates environmental and supply-chain challenges. Organic electrode materials (OEMs) reduce this reliance and provide broad molecular tunability. However, OEM-based batteries still show limited long-term cycling stability. Their design also requires the joint optimization of coupled metrics such as voltage, specific capacity, capacity retention, and energy density. These metrics depend on the full battery stack and on the interactions among its components rather than on the active material alone. In our previous work, we developed a data-fusion multi-task framework for average discharge voltage and first-cycle specific capacity. Both targets are single-valued. Here, we extend that framework to multi-horizon prediction by predicting a property at every cycle of a discharge trajectory rather than at a single cycle. Our multi-fidelity and Multi-horizon Deep Operator Network learns DFT redox potentials and cycle-dependent specific-capacity trajectories within one model. We train it on complete battery-stack representations and usage conditions, so it learns battery-stack interactions rather than cathode-only effects. This framework supports long-term property prediction, inverse design, and process optimization for organic battery systems.

title: Stiffness coefficients in granular micromechanics determined with three-point bending experiments and digital image correlation for a bimodulus material
abstract: This study presents an inverse analysis to determine the stiffness parameters of a bimodulus constitutive model formulated within a granular micromechanics framework. Full-field normal strain measurements are obtained by Digital Image Correlation (DIC) during three-point bending tests and are used as experimental input to a hybrid numerical optimization procedure. The experimental campaign is designed to ensure that the measured strain fields remain within the elastic regime. Since the identification is formulated as a nonlinear regression problem, a physically informed initial parameter set is constructed to guide the optimization toward mechanically meaningful values. An initial estimate of the compressive stiffness is first obtained from the available manufacturer data. The tension-compression stiffness asymmetry is then estimated from the experimentally measured neutral-axis shift, which provides a macroscopic signature of bimodulus material behavior in bending. These estimates define the initial parameter set, which is subsequently refined through a hybrid optimization procedure based on the full-field comparison of the experimental and numerical normal strain distributions. The identified parameter set enables the numerical model to reproduce more closely both the through-depth profile and the spatial distribution of the normal strain component over the selected surface region. These results demonstrate that full-field normal strain measurements provide an effective basis for identifying the stiffness parameters of bimodulus granular micromechanics models. The largest differences between the numerical and experimental strain fields are observed near the load-application region, where localized strain variations are induced by the concentrated load.

title: 'Porous anchor' that strongly bonds dissimilar materials formed simply by coating and drying
abstract: The National Institute for Materials Science has developed a technology to strongly bond dissimilar materials by using a porous layer, formed by a solution-coating and drying process, as an anchor. The research team confirm that even materials that are normally difficult to bond together can be bonded with a strength exceeding 7 MPa by adopting a hybrid approach: adhering to one material through chemical affinity and bonding to another via physical interlocking using tiny pores.

title: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
abstract: Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: The AtomicLimits Database: Towards Artificial Intelligence as a Research Assistant for Atomic Layer Deposition and Etching
abstract: The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. In this perspective, we propose a framework to evolve AtomicLimits into an AI-ready knowledge infrastructure that integrates literature-extracted, experimental, and simulation data through a community-defined schema, a structured template that specifies which data fields to capture and how to organize them. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.

title: Symmetry-Broken Co3O4 via Site-Selective Pd Substitution for Bifunctional Water Electrolysis
abstract: Spinel oxides generally show subpar activity for electrochemical water splitting because of low electronic conductivity, suboptimal adsorption energies, and poor operational stability. To overcome these limitations, Pd2+ is introduced to induce lattice strain in a metastable Co3O4 phase featuring off-centered cobalt and oxygen atoms. While pristine Co3O4 typically crystallizes in the centrosymmetric Fd3̅m space group, 1.2 at % Pd transforms it to the dominant non-centrosymmetric F4̅3m space group.

title: Potential antimalarial compound discovered in institute's microbe collection
abstract: Scientists hunting for a new malaria treatment may have found a solution within a historical natural compound collection housed at The Herbert Wertheim UF Scripps Institute for Biomedical Innovation & Technology.

title: Sustainable Design of Deep Eutectic Solvent Viscosity: A Structure–Property Machine Learning Framework with Structure-Disjoint Validation
abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DES) have emerged as sustainable alternatives to conventional organic solvents, yet their industrial adoption remains hindered by limited predictive capability for transport properties, particularly viscosity. This work reports a machine learning framework for DES viscosity prediction built on 3440 experimental measurements spanning 237 systems (85 hydrogen bond acceptors, 86 hydrogen bond donors), with viscosities from 1.3 to 85,000 mPa·s over 278–378 K, in which component identity is defined by canonical isomeric SMILES rather than by name and structural assignments have been audited and corrected. A hierarchical feature engineering strategy generated 236 candidate descriptors, reduced to 128 modeling features by removing noncomputable, monotonically redundant and collinear terms, with no imputation of missing values at any stage. Ten algorithms spanning linear, kernel, neural and tree-ensemble families were benchmarked under identical tuning and evaluation; support vector regression achieved the lowest cross-validated error (R2 = 0.974, AARD = 12.2%) against 42% for linear models, establishing that nonlinearity accounts for two-thirds of the achievable error reduction. The central result is a quantified separation between interpolation and extrapolation obtained on identical data and a single model: AARD is 13% on a random hold-out, 75% for an unseen acceptor under structure-disjoint leave-one-HBA-out validation, 129% for an unseen donor, and 145% for an unseen chemical family. This 10-fold spread demonstrates that a single reported accuracy figure is uninterpretable for DES property models unless the splitting protocol is stated. Global SHAP attribution on the final model assigns 31.4% of total contribution to composition-weighted mixing descriptors and 23.7% to asymmetry descriptors quantifying HBA–HBD dissimilarity, establishing both families as substantial and nonredundant. The framework integrates gradient-free inverse design on a smooth surrogate, application-oriented clustering by viscosity and Arrhenius activation energy, and manufacturing robustness assessment, providing actionable tools for rational DES formulation together with explicit and empirically measured boundaries on their use.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: The ACVR1C-GAS6 Antagonistic Axis Drives Metabolic Decompensation and Liver Fibrosis in MASLD: Mechanistic Insights from Multi-omics Analyses
abstract: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide, and liver fibrosis stage is the strongest determinant of long-term morbidity and mortality in affected patients. However, the molecular switches driving the transition from compensated steatosis to progressive fibrogenesis remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of early diagnostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic interventions.

title: Independent evolution of harmala alkaloids in medicinal Syrian rue and ayahuasca plants
abstract: Plants from distantly related lineages can produce identical neuroactive molecules, many of which have been independently adopted across human societies for their medicinal and cognition-altering effects. This phenomenon is exemplified by the traditional use of Syrian rue (Peganum harmala) and the ayahuasca vine (Banisteriopsis caapi) for medicine and ritual. Despite diverging over 100 million years ago and inhabiting different continents and climates, both plants synthesize harmala alkaloids (HAs), which inhibit human monoamine oxidase and exhibit diverse neuroactive effects. Here, we combine gene expression analyses, genomics, and enzyme characterization to elucidate HA biosynthesis for both Syrian rue and ayahuasca vine. We reveal multiple layers of biochemical and genetic convergence in these pathways, including independent duplication and neofunctionalization of an ancestral enzyme from serotonin biosynthesis, and lineage-specific repurposing of primary metabolic genes to generate a reactive precursor for alkaloid scaffold formation. Our study resolves biosynthetic routes to HAs in two medicinal plants and demonstrates convergent evolution of specialized metabolism at the levels of enzymes, pathways, and genomes.

title: Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design
abstract: Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation of 3D molecular graphs that align with predefined pharmacophore hypotheses. Through comprehensive testing, PharmaDiff demonstrates superior performance in matching 3D pharmacophore constraints compared to ligand-based drug design methods. Additionally, it achieves higher docking scores across a range of proteins in structure-based drug design, without the need for target protein structures. By integrating pharmacophore modeling with 3D generative techniques, PharmaDiff offers a powerful and flexible framework for rational drug design.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy for food safety analysis: sample presentation, data interpretation, and application readiness
abstract: Food-safety decisions require rapid screening of adulteration, origin fraud, elemental contamination and freshness loss. Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) provides direct multi-element fingerprints with short acquisition times and little reagent consumption. Its performance in foods, however, depends on a coupled analytical chain: sample presentation controls laser coupling and mass removal; plasma evolution and acquisition govern emission; calibration and modelling determine interpretation; and validation establishes reliability beyond the development dataset.

title: Studies on a luminescent antimicrobial metal complex reveal a method to directly image pathogenic bacterial infection in a living organism using optical microscopy
abstract: Methods to render Galleria Mellonella larvae transparent allowing three-dimensional viewing of larvae through orthodox light microscopy techniques are reported. To explore this models capability, we exploited the imaging properties of a metal complex antimicrobial to probe its therapeutic action against a pathogenic Acetinobacter baumannii infection. To illustrate the general utility of this method, we have also used the commercial fluorescent dye, Alexafluor-488, to image bacteria within live larvae.

title: Interplay of Synthesis, Structure and Thermoelectric Properties in Two Families of Silicide Zintl Phases Grown in Magnesium-Rich Flux
abstract: Large crystals of metal silicide Zintl phases with general formula (Ca/Eu/Mg)2Si were grown from reactions of silicon with varying amounts of europium and calcium in magnesium/zinc flux. The Eu/Ca reactant ratio determined the structure type of the products. Calcium-rich reactions yielded Ca1−xEuxMgSi (0 < x < 0.7) compounds adopting the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure type in space group Pnma. Increasing europium content led to the prevalence of Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (0 < y < 3.4) products with the hexagonal Ho5Ni19P12 structure type in space group P6̅2m.

title: Structure-Directing Agents of Chaordic Materials Using High-Entropy Alloying
abstract: For nearly a century, alloy design has been guided by the Hume-Rothery rules, which describe the conditions required for solid solution formation and have traditionally constrained the compositional space available to materials scientists. The emergence of high-entropy alloys fundamentally altered this paradigm by demonstrating that configurational entropy can stabilize compositions that would otherwise be thermodynamically unfavorable. Since their discovery, high-entropy concepts have expanded beyond metallic systems into ceramics, including oxides, carbides, silicides, nitrides, and borides, creating new opportunities to access unconventional chemistries and local atomic environments. This review examines how high-entropy alloying can be used to transcend classical alloying limitations and stabilize elements in coordination environments that are inaccessible in conventional materials. Particular emphasis is placed on high-entropy borides, where ordered boron frameworks provide a structural scaffold that accommodates chemically disparate elements while preserving phase stability. Recent examples, including Pt- and Si-containing high-entropy diborides, demonstrate how entropy stabilization enables the incorporation of elements that do not form stable binary diborides (MB2), resulting in unique electronic structures, bonding environments, and functional properties. More broadly, these systems illustrate how the interplay between disorder and local order can be leveraged to design next-generation materials beyond the boundaries imposed by traditional alloying rules.

title: Design Trade-Offs between Target Binding and Self-Association Revealed by De Novo SARS-CoV-2 Binders
abstract: De novo protein binders have emerged as a powerful platform for molecular recognition, yet achieving high affinity while maintaining favorable biophysical properties remains a major challenge. Here, using the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) as a model target, we generated two de novo protein binder design campaigns that deliberately imposed different trade-offs between binding and monomeric behavior, and benchmarked them against a set of experimentally validated binders. Through integrated experimental and computational analyses, we show that binder design is constrained by two distinct failure modes that require different optimization strategies. None of the 22 original designs showed measurable binding to the RBD, with one class remaining monomeric but failing to achieve sufficient target binding, while the other had more competent binding interfaces but exhibited excessive surface hydrophobicity that promoted self-association. By integrating AlphaFold-based predictions, molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and surface aggregation propensity (SAP) calculations, we establish complementary computational signatures that distinguish these failure modes and reveal their underlying structural determinants. Guided by these insights, we prospectively redesigned a representative failed binder by reducing noninterface hydrophobicity while preserving folding and binding interface quality. Experimental characterization by SEC-MALS, surface plasmon resonance, and circular dichroism confirmed that the redesigned variants were stable monomers and acquired low μM binding affinities. Together, our results define the mechanistic trade-offs between binding and self-association in de novo protein binder design and provide a framework for diagnosing and rationally overcoming common design failure modes.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Hierarchical Zeolites: Synthesis Strategies, Crystallization Mechanisms, and Machine Learning
abstract: The revelation of the crystallization mechanism of zeolites is the key to shifting their synthesis from trial-and-error methods to predictive approaches. This review introduces the traditional and recently emerging green synthesis methods of hierarchical zeolites and compares their crystallization mechanisms from the perspective of synthesis strategies. Then, by discussing the classical and nonclassical theories, it analyzes the crystallization mechanisms of different synthesis strategies for hierarchical zeolites and finds that the research on kinetic control methods not only conforms to the…

title: Application of PDE emulators for a multi-material, multi-physics simulation problem
abstract: Machine learning (ML) architectures are being developed for fast emulation of numerical simulators to accelerate both scientific discovery and engineering design. While these approaches are well-tested on popular PDE (partial differential equation) benchmarks, it is necessary to evaluate their performance on datasets that more accurately reflect industrial and engineering applications. We evaluate several computer vision-based architectures trained as surrogate models on a challenging computational physics task involving multiple materials, revealing significant implementation challenges for adapting certain pre-trained models, including transformer-based architectures. For such multi-physics multi-material datasets, our results underscore the importance of learning algorithms designed for sparse and imbalanced data, techniques for adapting spatial encodings and physical consistency metrics, in addition to methods for reducing the cost of generating sufficient training data.

title: Achieving Stable High-Voltage All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries: Electrolytes, Interfaces, and Advanced Characterization
abstract: Integrating the intrinsic safety of solid-state electrolytes and the high energy density enabled by high-voltage cathodes, high-voltage all-solid-state lithium batteries (HV-ASSLBs) have emerged as one of the most promising next-generation energy storage technologies. However, their practical application is hindered by the limited electrochemical stability windows of solid electrolytes and the complex physicochemical degradation reactions at the electrode-electrolyte interfaces.

title: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
abstract: Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Regioselective Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
abstract: Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Tiny droplets use pressure to unlock new routes to degradable plastics
abstract: Using a new technique, a research group led by Osaka Metropolitan University (OMU) has substantially increased the range of plastics that can be degraded naturally. The study is published in the journal Macromolecules.

title: Exploiting Differences in Molecular Interactions for Selective PFAS Separation from Natural Organic Matter during Ion-Exchange Regeneration
abstract: Ion-exchange resins effectively remove per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from water but generate concentrated brines co-loaded with natural organic matter, complicating downstream PFAS destruction. Here, we present a sequential selective regeneration strategy exploiting differences in adsorption mechanism and desorption kinetics between PFAS and humic substances to recover them in separate streams.

title: Distinct modes of N-terminal remodeling through a conserved inhibitor pocket in connexin-46/50
abstract: Selective pharmacological control of gap junction communication remains challenging because existing small-molecule connexin inhibitors act across multiple isoforms. The structural basis of this broad activity remains incompletely understood. Here, we used single-particle cryo-electron microscopy to examine native connexin-46/50 gap junction channels treated with two commonly used and chemically distinct inhibitors, 2-aminoethoxydiphenyl borate (2-APB) and carbenoxolone (CBX). Both treatments perturb the hydrophobic N-terminal (NT)-docking groove, but produce distinct conformational ensembles. 2-APB yields ordered destabilized-open and gated NT states resembling conformations observed during physiological pH- and Ca2+-dependent gating, with ligand- and lipid-associated densities accompanying the gated state. In contrast, CBX-compatible density occupies the same groove and is associated with loss of an ordered NT conformation, consistent with steric competition and altered physicochemical complementarity at the NT-docking site. Comparison with inhibitor-treated connexin-32 and connexin-36 structures identifies this region as a structurally conserved, pharmacologically sensitive pocket. These findings reveal how chemically diverse inhibitors perturb a conserved element of the native gating machinery while producing divergent NT-gating ensembles, providing a structural rationale for broad cross-isoform activity and identifying sequence-variable pocket margins that may support more selective modulation.

title: One-Pot Chemobiological Degradation, Bioassimilation, and Upcycling of Waste Poly(lactic acid)
abstract: Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) is the most widely produced biobased and biodegradable plastic with significant potential to address the plastics sustainability crisis. However, its current lifecycle is typically linear, with the majority of postconsumer PLA entering municipal waste streams or, at best, industrial composting. We hypothesized that the innate biodegradability of PLA and its terminal degradation product, lactate, offers an unexplored opportunity for biological upcycling into industrially valuable chemicals using engineered microbes. Herein, we report an operationally simple and low cost one-pot system for degradation and biological upcycling of waste PLA into the platform chemical protocatechuic acid (PCA). This is enabled by a novel method for PLA hydrolysis in unmodified microbial growth media at neutral pH with moderate heating (90 °C), achieving 85% depolymerization into lactate, showing a previously unreported synergistic mechanism involving phosphate and ammonium chloride. We further demonstrate compatibility with two examples of postconsumer PLA waste, 3D printing waste and food container lids, as well as showing the versatility of this method through degradation of four other biodegradable polyesters. Finally, we show that crude PLA hydrolysate can be directly inoculated with engineered Escherichia coli for bioproduction of PCA, achieving maximum titers of 1.05 mM PCA from authentic 3D printing waste. This study demonstrates, for the first time, that PLA-derived lactate can serve as the sole carbon source for growth and bioproduction using an engineered bacterium, highlighting the potential of biodegradable, next-generation plastic waste as a novel feedstock for chemical biomanufacturing.

title: Thermal laser evaporation of superconducting Nb films
abstract: Thermal laser evaporation (TLE) is an emerging physical vapor deposition (PVD) technique that uses continuous-wave lasers to evaporate even the most refractory elements. The deposition and characterization of superconducting refractory elements are of interest to assess the quality of films deposited by TLE. Here, we report the deposition of niobium (Nb) on c-plane sapphire using a home-built TLE system equipped with a 1070 nm continuous-wave fiber laser. A deposition rate of 0.19 Å/s was achieved with 533 W of laser power focused to a diameter of approximately 500 $μ$m on a Nb target. A film with a thickness of $22.47 \pm 0.05$ nm and a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of $0.23 \pm 0.02$ nm exhibited a room-temperature resistivity of $21.60 \pm 0.05$ $μΩ\mathrm{cm}$ and a residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) of 5.71. The superconducting transition temperature, $T_\mathrm{c}$, of the film was measured as 9.24 K, only 10 mK below the bulk value, with a transition width of 29 mK. Among films deposited without substrate heating, the electrical and superconducting properties of the present films meet or exceed those deposited by other techniques. This work contributes to the emerging consensus regarding TLE as a versatile PVD method for refractory elements and compounds.

title: Embodied timing turns a robotic tug-of-war into cooperative transport
abstract: Living systems move loads with agents that pull against one another. Kinesin and dynein pull one vesicle, ants haul a dead insect, and antagonist muscles move a joint. Whether the timing of the forces can, by itself, determine which side moves the load is not well understood. Here, combining experiments, theory, and simulations of a tug-of-war between two matched teams of spring-coupled robots, we show that the relative timing of the pull forces breaks the symmetry and decides the contest. Teams pulling in unison or in strict alternation tie. Between these, the lagging team wins, most strongly near a quarter cycle, because the springs unload while the leading team coasts and the lagging team still pulls. In the model and in robot simulations, braking rather than coasting between pulls, once strong enough, shifts the advantage to the leading team. Winning and losing leave distinct signatures in each robot's motor current. Using these local signals, we formulate an embodied decentralized phase-adaptation rule that enables transient leadership to switch between teams, allowing the collective to transport high-friction cargo and to navigate around obstacles towards a prescribed target without explicit communication.

title: Multivalency in endocytic accessory proteins orchestrates membrane shape transitions
abstract: Fast endophilin-mediated endocytosis (FEME) relies on the coordinated activities of membrane-remodeling proteins and multivalent protein interaction networks. Endophilin is a potent membrane curvature generator through its N-BAR domain and forms multivalent interactions with the proline-rich motifs (PRMs) of lamellipodin via its SH3 domain. Although these interactions are known to promote biomolecular condensation, their functional consequences for membrane remodeling have remained unclear.

title: From a Lifshitz Transition to Spin-Density-Wave Order: Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ under Uniaxial Strain
abstract: In recent years, the effects of uniaxial strain on Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ have been extensively investigated, revealing a pronounced enhancement of the superconducting critical temperature accompanied by experimental indications of an emergent magnetically ordered state. In this Letter, we study the impact of strain on the spectral and magnetic properties of this material within an advanced many-body theoretical framework. We find that strain induces an anisotropic Lifshitz transition, which enhances the electron scattering rate along the elongation axis while simultaneously promoting coherent Fermi-liquid behavior in the perpendicular direction, in close agreement with experimental observations. Taking into account this anisotropic behavior allows us to capture the magnetic instability leading to a finite-temperature ordered state at large strain values. Our analysis further reveals that the magnetic response is dominated by two competing wave vectors associated with distinct nesting vectors: one within the $γ$ sheet and the other between the $α$ and $β$ sheets of the Fermi surface. Both wave vectors can stabilize magnetic order, with their competition depending sensitively on the coherence of the respective Fermi surface sheets.

title: Characterizing statistical association patterns and local forecasting of PM2.5-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon concentrations in Nagoya, Japan
abstract: This study developed an integrated pollutant-meteorology-polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) statistical framework using association rule mining and machine learning to characterize the hourly variability of PAHs bound to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in Nagoya, Japan. Association rules identified recurring pollutant-meteorology co-occurrence patterns linked to PAH accumulation, while machine learning models, evaluated via time-blocked cross-validation to avoid leakage from hourly autocorrelation, enabled short-term prediction.

title: A 'simple recipe' takes some of the guesswork out of mass spectrometry imaging
abstract: A small sample of human tissue can hold a remarkable amount of information. Researchers can use it to search for molecular clues associated with cancer, investigate the chemical landscape of the brain or determine where a drug travels after it enters the body. Mass spectrometry imaging, or MSI, helps answer those questions by mapping where different molecules are located within tissue.

title: Pretrained graph transformer-driven de novo design and machine learning prioritization of computationally predicted ENR-InhA (InhA) inhibitors with potential relevance to drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis
abstract: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) undermines frontline therapy, and conventional drug discovery is slow and resource intensive. We present an integrated computational pipeline for the de novo design of inhibitors of a single clinically validated target, the NADH-dependent enoyl-[acyl-carrier-protein] reductase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (ENR-InhA, encoded by inhA). Bioactive compounds were retrieved from ChEMBL and curated to 80 with equality-qualified IC50 values.
venue: SAR and QSAR in environmental research

title: Discovering Underpotentially Deposited Crystalline Sodium Metal Nanoparticles on the Surface of Hard Carbon Anodes
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries are attractive candidates for low-cost and scalable energy storage in which hard carbon (HC) anodes are used. However, sodium (Na) metal plating in HC anodes at voltages above the plating potential remains a critical problem. The location and spatial distribution of crystalline sodium (c-Na) metal nanoparticles, the clusters associated with Na storage in HCs, are important for understanding this underpotential plating behavior but remain unclear.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: NMR-measured Per-residue Electrostatic Potentials Reveal the Importance of Arginine-Lysine Balance on the Conformational Ensemble of Disordered Histone H3 Tails in Nucleosome Core Particles
abstract: Biophysical studies of chromatin have provided key insights into how the genome is regulated. Many atomic resolution structures of the fundamental building block of chromatin, the nucleosome core particle (NCP), as well as larger NCP arrays, both in isolation and in complex with effectors, or with post-translational modifications, have been elucidated. These provide in-depth pictures of key functional interactions.

title: Genetic control couples TGFβ-independent pluripotent stem cell renewal to deterministic forward programming across germ layers
abstract: Reproducible and scalable manufacture of human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) derivatives requires control over expansion and differentiation. Transcription factor-mediated forward programming can place hiPSC differentiation under genetic control, but expansion still relies on extracellular growth-factor supplementation, increasing process complexity and operator dependence. Here we introduce GERALT (Genetically Enhanced Renewal and Autonomous Lineage Transdifferentiation), a push-pull genetic circuit assembled through targeted safe-harbour integration that couples NANOG-supported, TGF{beta}-independent renewal to doxycycline-inducible lineage programming and simultaneous NANOG silencing. GERALT maintained pluripotency during extended TGF{beta} withdrawal in both adherent and suspension culture, yet remained programmable towards myogenic, neuronal, and hepatic fates. Compared with the established OPTi-OX platform in myogenesis, GERALT enabled differentiation in simplified medium while canalising and accelerating commitment. GERALT also supported direct myogenic programming in suspension and enabled direct casting of hiPSCs into hydrogel followed by in-tissue programming, yielding electrically responsive engineered muscle tissues. These results extend genetic control upstream into stem cell renewal, facilitating deployment of new approach methodologies and other biomanufacturing applications.

title: A Photosensitizer Bearing an Asymmetric “Push-Pull” Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
abstract: Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Dynamic Poly(disulfide) Interphase Enhances Ductility and Toughness of Covalent Adaptable Network Composite without Loss of Stiffness
abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) offer recyclability and reprocessability, yet bond-exchange dynamics can reduce mechanical strength and toughness. Although the composite formation of CAN provides benefits in both aspectsstrengthening the CAN and adding recyclability to the compositeit still faces a stiffness−ductility trade-off that limits material usefulness. Here, we demonstrate a CAN composite design in which silica nanoparticle incorporation, combined with interfacial chemical structure, enhances ductility and toughness in a highly crosslinked matrix without compromising the high elastic modulus. Introducing poly(disulfide) dynamic covalent bonding chains into the network and at the filler interface significantly increases ductility, toughness, and stress at break. Together with a comparison to composites with permanent interfacial bonding, these results underscore the important role of interfacial chemistry. Based on these comparative experiments, the observed toughness enhancement is proposed to arise from energy dissipation via reorganization at the interphase through stress-activated disulfide exchange and network topological rearrangement. The resulting stress-responsive viscoelasticity enables stable deformation and allows CAN-based composites to overcome the stiffness−ductility trade-off.

title: Geometry-Aware Molecular Representation Learning for Approximating NORMAN-Predicted Retention Time Indices in Nontargeted Screening
abstract: Retention information provides chromatographic evidence complementary to mass spectrometric data in LC-HRMS nontargeted screening (NTS), yet many existing models rely mainly on 1D SMILES or 2D molecular graphs and make limited use of three-dimensional structure. Here, we developed ViSRTI (Vector-Interaction-Spatial Retention Time Index), a ViSNet-based geometry-aware framework that integrates 3D molecular representations with multimodal descriptors to model the precomputed positive- and negative-mode RTI labels in NORMAN SusDat.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Machine learning based on behavioral, fecal and oocyst analyses for chicken coccidiosis diagnosis: A systematic review with exploratory extension
abstract: In the context of large-scale and intensive poultry farming, avian coccidiosis causes substantial economic losses. Timely and accurate diagnosis is essential for effective control and prevention. However, conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopic examination and molecular assays, are constrained by limited efficiency and a heavy reliance on specialized expertise, rendering them inadequate for real-time, high-throughput diagnosis in modern farming systems.

title: Drag racers and long haulers: the design space of myosin-V-like motor proteins
abstract: The ubiquitous myosin class-V molecular motors transport cellular cargo long distances at roughly 0.5 m/s. Plant-specific myosin class-XI motors share nearly identical structural features with myosin-V, yet display velocities from 0.25 to 70 m/s, the fastest transport motor in nature. Empirical observations suggest an inverse relationship between run length and velocity. These observations raise a central question: how can a single motor design support both highly processive "long-hauler" and extremely rapid "drag-racer" motors? We generalize a polymer-based model of force-dependent myosin-V dynamics to encompass the broader design space. The model quantitatively captures experimental data from fast myosin-XI and yields general analytical expressions for key observables. Notably, we derive a Pareto frontier that defines the trade-off between velocity and run distance, as well as the theoretical maximum velocity achievable by such motors. Our results establish the biological limits of natural and synthetic myosin-V-like motor design.

title: Multivalent Scaffolding by XIST E-Repeats Tunes RNA Binding Protein Cooperativity and Lowers the Phase Separation Threshold
abstract: The long-noncoding RNA XIST coordinates the random silencing of one X-chromosome in female placental mammals as a class of chromosomal dosage compensation across sexes. Critical to this process is the diffusion of XIST foci across the 155 Mb of the X-chromosome to achieve 96% repression. The E-Repeat domain on XIST primarily drives this process through the recruitment of several RNA-binding proteins, which seed condensate formation for controlled distal spreading. To date, there is a lack of biophysical characterization of interactions between the E-Repeats and its protein binding partners.

title: Steering Solid–Solution Equilibria to Tame Phase Complexity and Instability in Dion-Jacobson Quasi-2D Halide Perovskites
abstract: Dion-Jacobson (DJ) quasi-two-dimensional (2D) halide perovskites (HPs) have emerged as a robust platform for optoelectronic applications, yet their crystallization pathways and subsequent phase evolution remain insufficiently understood. Herein, we integrate robotic high-throughput synthesis with automated spectral diagnosis and multimodal characterization to investigate 1,4-butanediammonium-based HPs containing methylammonium (MA) or formamidinium (FA) across composition and temperature.

title: DBNAMP: A Chemically Curated Database of Noncanonical Antimicrobial Peptides with Standardized Molecular Representations
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising anti-infective agents, yet conventional sequence-centered resources often inadequately represent noncanonical residues, stereochemical variations, terminal modifications, cyclization, lipidation, stapling, and peptidomimetic scaffolds, limiting chemically meaningful annotation, comparison, and structure–activity relationship analysis.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Characterization of the Preclinical in Vitro and in Vivo Pharmacokinetic Properties of the Cyclic Oligomeric Depsipeptide Ryanodine Receptor 2 Inhibitor ent-Verticilide
abstract: ent-Verticilide is a synthetic cyclic oligomeric depsipeptide that inhibits ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2)-mediated calcium (Ca) leak and has demonstrated antiarrhythmic activity in mice. This study characterized the preclinical absorption, distribution, metabolism, and pharmacokinetic properties of ent-verticilide and investigated factors affecting its oral exposure. ent-Verticilide was stable in rat plasma and simulated gastric and intestinal fluids but exhibited extensive plasma protein binding (>94%) and low apparent permeability in Caco-2 cells, with no evidence of pronounced net efflux. In rat and human liver microsomes, ent-verticilide underwent rapid NADPH-dependent metabolism, with an in vitro half-life of 5.43 min and 4.35 min, respectively, and a predicted hepatic extraction ratio of 0.90 and 0.92, respectively. Following intravenous administration in rats, ent-verticilide exhibited a systemic clearance of 25.5 mL/min/kg and a large steady-state volume of distribution (4.72 L/kg). Absolute oral bioavailability was approximately 16%. Simultaneous portal and systemic sampling estimated intestinal availability (FaFg) at 0.25 and hepatic availability (Fh) at 0.64, suggesting that processes occurring before hepatic entry are a major limitation to oral exposure. Pretreatment with the CYP inhibitor 1-aminobenzotriazole increased portal and systemic exposure approximately 10.6- and 18.5-fold, respectively, and increased apparent Fh to approximately 1. Collectively, these findings identify limited intestinal availability and CYP-mediated presystemic metabolism as important determinants of ent-verticilide exposure and provide a framework for its continued development as an RyR2-targeted therapeutic.

title: Where the Error Lives: Spectral Representations of Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians
abstract: Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) is the standard method for computing the electronic structure of molecules and materials, but its self-consistent-field (SCF) iterations make it expensive for large systems and high-throughput screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonian models offer a shortcut: an equivariant network predicts the Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian matrix in one forward pass, and diagonalizing the prediction yields orbital energies, the HOMO-LUMO gap, molecular orbitals and the electron density. These models are trained to match the reference matrix entry by entry, yet a small entry-wise error does not guarantee accurate eigenvalues or eigenvectors. Two physics-informed alternatives go partway: a recently proposed wavefunction-alignment loss adds a spectral penalty without diagonalizing the prediction, and matching the electron density of the diagonalized prediction supervises it directly. Neither is complete: by representing the prediction error in the eigenbasis of the reference Hamiltonian, we show that each sees only part of the error, and that shifting the predicted orbital energies leaves the electron density exactly unchanged. The same analysis identifies a complete training signal: the cumulative local density of states (cumulative LDOS), the number of electrons at each point in space with energy below a given threshold. The cumulative LDOS is a single physical observable that contains the electron density as a special case, responds to every component of the error, determines the Hamiltonian uniquely, and yields gradients that do not vanish for large orbitalenergy errors. Fine-tuning three Hamiltonian networks on QH9 in this way, which we call FermiScope, reduces the HOMO-LUMO gap error without increasing the element-wise error. The gains carry over to out-of-distribution and molecular-dynamics splits, where the wavefunction-alignment loss helps less.

title: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback
abstract: Language-model agents differ fundamentally from prior intelligent systems in their ability to learn from natural language in context. This capability enables agents to iteratively refine their answers in response to feedback, a prevalent mode of operation in modern agentic workflows. However, the community primarily ranks models by metrics such as Pass@1 or Pass@K, which cannot capture how they utilize feedback on prior attempts. We introduce Seq@K, a natural evaluation protocol that measures whether a model can solve a problem within K sequential attempts, provided feedback after each previous failure. Unlike multi-turn agentic benchmarks that examine long-horizon planning, Seq@K isolates and formalizes the core capability of refinement from feedback. We evaluate Seq@K on a suite of 7 benchmarks and 16 frontier models, and show that Seq@K reveals a materially different model-selection landscape: under Seq@K, (1) model rankings often differ, (2) the Pareto frontiers admit more efficient configurations and (3) the gains from choosing the optimal model configuration can widen or shrink relative to those of Pass@K. We further show that analyzing model trajectories under Seq@K helps characterize iterative refinement behavior, such as the rate at which models address issues raised in feedback, or how rigidly they hold onto their own answers. Finally, we study how the nature of feedback affects models' iterative refinement, showing that practitioners must carefully design and benchmark the feedback loops of iterative agentic systems. Together, these results establish how Seq@K offers a more faithful metric for intelligent systems that typically operate in such feedback loop, and the necessity to consider Seq@K in evaluating models for these systems.

title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
abstract: Existing scientific-agent benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can reconstruct the exact molecular structures and generation workflows specified by sequencing protocols, a capability critical for analyzing customized sequencing assays. We introduce LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark for reconstructing sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows. Our experiments show that frontier agents often produce approximately correct reconstructions but remain unreliable at exact reconstruction, particularly in molecular-state representation and workflow connectivity. Switching the underlying language model produced larger average performance differences than switching agent harnesses, with a statistically significant difference only for molecular-state reconstruction. Additional knowledge improved oligo-family recovery in a small pilot without improving mean molecular-workflow scores. Autonomous accumulation of procedural rules and cross-protocol examples showed non-monotonic validation performance and no mean held-out molecular-workflow improvement in the tested trajectory. These findings highlight the need for more controlled and verifiable approaches to scientific reasoning about molecular processes in complex experimental protocols.

title: DropFENO: A Data-Free, Physics-Based Operator-Learning Framework for Droplet Equilibria on Mixed-Wettability Patterned Surfaces
abstract: We study whether the equilibrium of a drop on a chemically patterned wall, and the capillary forces that the pattern exerts on it, can be learned from the free energy alone, without solution data. We introduce DropFENO (Droplet Free-Energy Neural Operator), in which Fourier (FNO), tensor-factorised Fourier (TFNO) and wavelet (WNO) neural operators are trained in two and three dimensions on the diffuse-interface free energy of the drop, with its volume and centroid constraints imposed as penalties. The predictions are tested with the virtual-work (Hellmann--Feynman) theorem: the force exerted by the pattern on a held drop is a wall integral of the equilibrium field which, for a drop straddling a wettability step, reduces identically to the contact-line law $F=σΔ\cosθ\,L$. DropFENO reproduces this law and the energy landscape of a drop crossing a step, and reproduces the pinning of the receding contact line less accurately. The residual error lies in the soft modes of the capillary energy (small displacements of the interface and the contact line). This explains why the energy is predicted accurately while contact-line positions are not, and why on striped walls the operators return Cassie-like states instead of the edge-pinned states whose anisotropic apparent angles the reference minimiser shares with lattice Boltzmann simulations. On held-out patterned walls the median energy of the predictions lies $\NdEmedRandFnoTwo$ of the free-drop energy above the best known minimum (FNO, two dimensions), at about one hundredth of the cost of a per-instance minimisation, and a refinement by a classical solver started from the prediction returns the reference state in almost all cases.

title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
abstract: Equation learning seeks to discover compact, interpretable equations from data using various machine-learning techniques. However, few workflows discover and interpret learned equations in sparse, high-dimensional materials datasets. We present nn-EQL, an equation-learning framework that generates candidate equations through iterative training, pruning, and retraining of a neural network with customizable, user-specified neuron-level activation functions. Candidate equations are ranked using a minimum description length (MDL)-inspired score, balancing error and sparsity, and diagnosed to assess term-wise contributions, input-scaled sensitivities, and uncertainties. We demonstrate nn-EQL on standard AI-Feynman benchmarks as well as multiscale high-dimensional materials datasets such as finite-element simulations of heterogeneous materials, and high-throughput experimental thin-film deposition data. nn-EQL integrates with tabular data and high-dimensional data via standard encoder models, learning equations and providing insight into learned terms. Looking forward, integrating physically interpretable representations, multimodal and multi-fidelity data, and adaptive data acquisition could enable equation learning to formulate and test mechanistic hypotheses.

title: Spatial localization of magnetic-branch force contrasts in substitutional Mn-doped Ge: A first-principles study
abstract: Magnetic energy gaps do not reveal the spatial distribution of magnetic-state-dependent atomic forces. We compare ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic forces at identical nuclear positions in 64-site substitutional Mn-doped Ge using collinear PBE calculations. For nearest-neighbour Mn pairs, the radial force projection reverses sign between magnetic branches. In the second-neighbour geometry, the shared Ge neighbour has the largest force contrast, about 2.2 times that of equally near Ge sites coordinated to one Mn. Bridge-displacement gap slopes agree with direct force derivatives across four numerical settings. Tightening the electronic threshold by 100-fold preserves magnetic ordering and the leading site, while the force-contrast vector changes by 1.08% despite a nearly unchanged energy gap. The results identify coordination-associated localization of magnetic-branch force contrasts within the frozen model, without establishing relaxed distortions, full numerical convergence or a unique exchange mechanism.

title: Antisymmetric thermopower without magnetism in three-phase composites
abstract: A thermopower that turns a temperature gradient into a perpendicular electric field in every in-plane direction has relied on magnetism. Reciprocity permits it without magnetism, yet under a three-fold or higher axis it vanishes both in reciprocal elastic band transport and in composites of two isotropic phases with ideal interfaces. Here we show that composites of three isotropic phases carry it, and that under such an axis three is the minimum. A third, linearly independent transport matrix escapes the exact two-phase reduction; at weak contrast the first allowed axial term is cubic, proportional to a determinant of the three matrices times material-weighted, handed three-point correlations. Treating the phases as colours identifies the arrangements that allow the response, and crystal nets from reticular chemistry supply printable three-dimensional ones. Certified two-sided bounds give axial Seebeck coefficients of 49.5-50.2 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a planar cell and 76-84 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a printable woodpile; reflections in planes containing the axis reverse the response, and recolouring 24 nets to restore their parent symmetry switches it off. Around a line heat source the axial driving field has the $1/r$ azimuthal form of the magnetic field of a straight wire and drives circulating currents.

title: Neuronal Identity as an Organizational Basis for Analyzing Neural Population Dynamics
abstract: Individual neurons exhibit diverse molecular, morphological, and electrophysiological properties that shape their distinct roles in neural circuits. While these multimodal features are largely shared across individuals, they remain an underutilized source of information in analyzing neural population dynamics. We posit that these shared biological profiles provide a common reference for relating neural dynamics across subjects and recording sessions. Our framework leverages this structure by routing neurons into latent groups based on their biological profiles and analyzing population dynamics through group-level representations. Because these assignments are anchored in biological properties that are consistent across subjects, the learned organization supports transfer to unseen animals without retraining or neuron-wise correspondence. We evaluate our framework on whole-brain calcium imaging in larval zebrafish and large-scale electrophysiology in the mouse visual cortex. Across both species and recording modalities, the framework delivers state-of-the-art performance in both neural decoding and manifold analysis: it achieves superior decoding of behavior and stimulus labels while better preserving the temporal consistency and local geometric structure of latent trajectories on unseen data. Our experiments demonstrate that not only does providing biological features improve baseline performance, but our proposed framework achieves even stronger results by using these properties to explicitly structure the population rather than treating them as auxiliary inputs. Together, these results suggest that organizing neural populations by their multimodal biological features offers a promising framework for generalizing population dynamics across subjects and recording sessions.

title: ODAT-SE: A modular and parallel framework for simulation-based inverse problems
abstract: Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. It succeeds 2DMAT, which was developed for surface-structure analysis with quantum-beam diffraction and has since been applied to other fields. In version 3, the search algorithms were separated from the application-specific solvers, which became independent packages, and the software was renamed; this paper describes the current version 4.0. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions.
