Elastic slope, peak force and crack path therefore cannot be met practically by a single parameter set. The objective must be fixed for the calibration of the model parameters and reported together with the numerical parameters and the boundary value problem.

title: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification
abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. This work presents two compact spiking neural networks (SNNs) matched to their target hardware: ConvSNN, which maps to the Matrix Vector Processor (MVP) of an EFM32PG28 microcontroller, and StreamSNN, which processes one waveform value per timestep using learned time constants and fixed synaptic delays for a dedicated SKY130 circuit. Evaluated on cells unseen during training, ConvSNN achieves a CS F1 of 0.873 with 1,018 parameters and StreamSNN 0.837 with 527 parameters, both with eight-bit weights. On the microcontroller, MVP acceleration reduces ConvSNN latency by 62.3\% and extends estimated battery life to 33.73~hours on a 50~mAh battery. In SKY130, StreamSNN occupies 0.173~mm$^2$ and consumes 0.46~$μ$J per event, with 0.2~ms of computation within an 8.3~ms end-to-end latency.

title: Cu intercalation and field-driven filament formation in vertically aligned MoS$_2$ memristors
abstract: Vertically-aligned MoS$_2$ films paired with a Cu top electrode have been used as electrochemical metallization cell memristor devices. The memristive switching has been attributed to the formation of conductive filaments, yet their exact structure has remained elusive. Here we carry out a multi-scale computational study of Cu intercalation, clustering, and field-driven dynamics to eventually model the filament formation under operating conditions. We use density-functional theory results to fine-tune a machine learning force field, and the most important physical phenomena are further distilled into multi-particle kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. By exhaustive enumeration of Cu intercalated structures, we find the most stable structure at MoS$_2$Cu$_{0.11}$ composition, with Cu atoms forming a dice lattice between the MoS$_2$ layers. These structures are shown to exhibit metallic character and can thus form conductive filaments under memristor operation. The simulated switching speed and threshold voltage agree well with the available experimental data. Our results give fundamental insights on the device operation mechanism and guidelines for maximizing switching speed and endurance.

title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission
abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevant biological context. A domain-specific ontology organizes 14 evidence types into five categories: Zoonotic Surveillance, Transmission Evidence, Experimental Infection, Functional Mechanism, and Genomic Evolution. The platform integrates ontology-guided curation, large language model-assisted literature screening and candidate extraction, automated consistency checks, and curator review of flagged or ambiguous records, enabling daily updates. As of 4 August 2026, OmniVira contained 8072 publicly retrievable OVE records derived from 2623 source articles, spanning 60 ICTV virus families, 55 host orders, and 121 countries. Its responsive interface supports evidence-centred retrieval, source-text verification, and exploration of linked virus-host-literature relationships across desktop and mobile browsers. OmniVira provides a transparent, context-preserving resource for systematic comparison and synthesis of evidence related to zoonotic viral emergence and cross-species transmission.

title: Carboxylation of Bio-Based 2-Furoic Acid with CO2 to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid over CuAlO x Catalysts
abstract: Direct C–H carboxylation with CO2 as a renewable C1 source stands out as an atom-economical strategy for CO2 utilization. However, the low reactivity of C–H bond and intrinsic inertness of CO2 limit carboxylation efficiency. This work presents a cooperative CuAlOx-Cs2CO3 catalytic system for the C–H carboxylation of 2-furoic acid (FA) with CO2 to produce 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (2,5-FDCA), a key bio-based monomer for polyethylene furanoate (PEF).

title: Surface-engineered nanostructured adsorbents for CO2 capture: From material design to process integration and industrial deployment
abstract: The growing necessity to curb CO2 emissions from man-made sources has driven the development of highly efficient and economical approaches to carbon capture. The current review is intended to give an overview and critical analysis of nanomaterial-based adsorbents for CO2 capture with specific consideration of the connections between nanomaterial properties, adsorption processes, process integration, and industrial application. As opposed to the majority of literature surveys, which concentrate on either certain classes of materials or adsorption capacity of various materials separately, the review proposes a holistic view by combining information on the correlations of pore structure, surface chemistry, thermodynamics, adsorption kinetics, selectivity principles, and regeneration behavior of different nanostructured adsorbents, such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), hierarchical nanoporous carbons, graphene analogs, silica hybrids, metal oxides, and bioinspired materials. Special focus is paid to surface engineering of adsorbents, including amine grafting, heteroatom doping, and compositing, and its influence on CO2 affinity, cyclic stability, and transport properties of adsorbents. Apart from the lab-scale efficiency, it analyzes issues of scale-up, regeneration efficiency, process intensification, techno-economic viability, and life-cycle sustainability. New possibilities such as machine-learning aided design of new adsorbents, standardized performance measures, and the concept of circular economy are also discussed. This review acts as a guideline and framework for designing nanostructured adsorbents that can be used in carbon management on a large scale.

title: Multireference Second-Order Perturbation Theories Based on Iterative Configuration Interaction with Selection
abstract: Under the assumption that the static correlation can well be described by selected configuration interaction, to the extent that the residual dynamic correlation can be accounted for accurately by a second-order perturbation theory (PT2), a family of multireference PT2s (iCI-MRPT2) based on the iterative configuration interaction with selection are proposed and compared. The first step is to partition a large complete active space (CAS) $P$ into the direct sum of a primary ($P_m$) and a secondary ($P_s$) subspace via a parameter $C_{\mathrm{min}}$. The former serves as the actual reference space, whereas the latter is treated via Epstein-Nesbet PT2. An MRPT2 is then invoked to account for the dynamic correction of the $Q=1-P$ space to the $P_m$ space. Different MRPT2s are distinguished by the underlying zeroth-order Hamiltonians. To circumvent the prohibitive computational cost and memory footprint associated with high-order reduced density matrices in the fully internally contracted scheme and the exponential growth of external functions (XF) in the uncontracted scheme, a partial contraction strategy is employed for constructing the XFs: those involving one or two inactive (core or virtual) orbitals are kept uncontracted, whereas those involving three or four inactive orbitals are internally contracted. They span the uncontracted ($Q_u$) and contracted ($Q_c$) portions of $Q$, respectively. The former is further split into two subspaces $Q_u^c$ and $Q_u^u$ via a parameter $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$, which are to be treated in coupled and uncoupled manners, respectively. Extrapolations to zero $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{min}}$ can be performed, so as to approach CAS-based MRPT2. Calculations with active spaces as large as CAS(56e,58o) can now be performed. The size-consistency of the iCI-MRPT2s is also analyzed in detail.

title: Magnetic crystal generation with site-resolved magnetic moments via Gaussian-mixture retargeting and finite-budget yield prediction
abstract: We introduce GMMag, a workflow for generating crystal structures together with their site-resolved magnetic moments, built on a conditional variational autoencoder with a graph neural network encoder and a transformer decoder. Gaussian-mixture sampling redirects generation towards selected chemical and magnetic targets without retraining. We systematically investigate how encoder and decoder design, the representation of magnetic-moment magnitudes and relative signs, and sampling choices affect reconstruction, generation quality and diversity. Because a higher screening pass rate does not necessarily yield more qualifying candidates with distinct chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, we model how repeated generation of the same chemical formulas limits their accumulation and test the model in two separate ten-million-draw runs. As an application, the workflow identifies Nd-containing candidates with chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, negative formation energies and high estimated saturation magnetization.

title: Enhancing magneto-optical coupling and scattering from magnetic vortices by optical polarization texturing
abstract: Magnetic textures offer a route toward photonic functionality in which electromagnetic fields are controlled not only by material composition and geometry but also by the internal magnetic configuration. Conversely, spatial texturing of these fields is a qualitatively new tool to increase the effective coupling strength to magnetic matter and to act on the the vortex topology and magnetic dynamics. Here, we investigate the coupling and scattering of structured electromagnetic fields by a magnetic vortex, focusing on how spatially non-collinear magnetization governs polarization conversion, electromagnetic energy flow, and magnetization dynamics. We develop a spherical rigorous coupled-wave method that incorporates the spatially dependent anisotropic magnetic permeability associated with the vortex texture. The calculations show that the off-diagonal components of the magnetic susceptibility mediate conversion into complementary polarization channels that are absent from the incident field. The generated fields exhibit pronounced spatial localization associated with the vortex magnetization profile and support a nonzero azimuthal component of electromagnetic energy flow. A comparison between linearly and radially polarized illumination reveals an approximately one-order-of-magnitude difference in the scattered fields amplitudes due to polarization texturing, demonstrating the importance of spatial overlap between the incident field and the anisotropic magnetic response. The back-action on the magnetic vortex dynamics is quantitatively demonstrated by numerical simulations for the inverse Faraday effect due to the rectification of structured effective-field excitation. It is shown that polarization textured optical fields can drive vortex-core precession and, at sufficiently strong excitation, reverse the core polarity and chirality on nanosecond time scale.

title: Hepatocyte nuclear factor-1β recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase complex to activate gene transcription
abstract: Mutations affecting the transcription factor hepatocyte nuclear factor-1{beta} (HNF-1{beta}) are the most common monogenic cause of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. The mechanism whereby HNF-1{beta} regulates gene transcription remains unclear. Here, we performed an unbiased proteomic screen and found that endogenous HNF-1{beta} interacts with core subunits of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase complex (NuRD) in renal epithelial cells.

title: Organometallic complexes as donors and non-fullerene acceptors for organic solar cells: DFT-guided design, structure-property relationships, and future directions
abstract: Computational screening has become indispensable to organic solar cell (OSC) design, allowing the electronic, optical, and charge-transport properties of a candidate to be predicted before synthesis. Organometallic complexes (OMCs) are especially well suited to this approach: their metal centers offer design handles-tunable frontier-orbital energies, strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC), and metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) transitions that purely organic semiconductors lack. Long confined to donor and interlayer roles, OMCs have recently emerged as credible non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) once functionalized with electron-withdrawing groups, yet their donor and acceptor chemistries have been reviewed in isolation rather than within a common density functional theory (DFT) framework. This review examines how DFT and its time-dependent extension (TD-DFT) guide the design of OMCs that function as both donors and NFAs. We assess the prevailing computational protocols-hybrid and range-separated functionals (B3LYP, CAM-B3LYP, ωB97XD, M06-2X), effective core potentials (LANL2DZ), and continuum solvation models (PCM, SMD) and the descriptors that link molecular structure to device performance: frontier molecular orbital (FMO) energies, reorganization and exciton-binding energies, and SOC matrix elements. The literature is organized by metal center-ferrocene (Fe), iridium (Ir), platinum (Pt), ruthenium (Ru), osmium (Os), and metalloporphyrin/phthalocyanine systems. Across the surveyed systems, DFT-computed band gaps reproduce experimental trends well, and an optimal acceptor LUMO window of -3.5 to -3.9 eV emerges. Within this window, we rationalize the record power conversion efficiencies of 19.24% (ternary Pt-based) and 15.25% (ternary Cu-porphyrin) devices. We distill these findings into transferable, metal-specific design rules alongside a candid assessment of method reliability. We close by charting the integration of machine learning with high-throughput DFT toward OMC-NFAs that exceed 20% efficiency with improved operational stability.

title: A machine learning framework for polymeric nanoparticle design with zero-shot generalization across active pharmaceutical ingredients
abstract: The development of polymeric nanoparticles remains largely empirical, requiring extensive experimental screening to identify suitable formulation and processing conditions for each active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). Machine learning (ML) offers opportunities to support data-driven drug-delivery development, but existing approaches are often restricted to individual compounds and lack external validation.

title: The role of A in ARPES
abstract: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was developed in the 1970s-1990s as a momentum-resolved probe of the electronic structure of solids, with its basic principles summarized in early seminal works and classic reviews. The basic ARPES result is currently almost exclusively associated with the two-dimensional intensity distribution with coordinate axes labeled as Binding Energy and Momentum. Such datasets are usually directly compared to the band structure calculations along high symmetry directions of the Brillouin zone. Here we show that this is the result of an oversimplified treatment of the ARPES data leading to incorrect interpretations of the experimental results. We suggest practical ways of how to avoid it in both data collection and analysis.

title: Effects of Zeolite Framework on Direct Reduction of Esters to Ethers Using H2 on Pt-Zeolite Catalysts
abstract: The direct reduction of esters to ethers using H2 represents a fundamental selectivity challenge for heterogeneous catalysis and offers a method to increase the hydrothermal stability of chemicals and fuels derived from renewable resources. Prior studies revealed that ethers derive from a series of reactions that involve in situ formation of hemiacetals by hydrogen transfer on metal nanoparticles, followed by diffusive transport to Brønsted acid sites that cleave the carbonyl C–O bond. The competing hydrogenolysis pathway proceeds by a similar bifunctional mechanism; however, hydrolysis and transesterification occur by direct reactions of esters solely at Brønsted acid sites. Here, we find that rates and selectivities reflect the intrinsic reactivity at individual Brønsted acid sites, which depends upon the topology of the aluminosilicate support. Pt-Faujasite (FAU) provides ether formation rates at least an order of magnitude greater than smaller pore zeolites that possess similar Pt loadings and Si/Al ratios (e.g., mordenite framework inverted (MFI), beta (BEA), and ferrierite (FER)). Correlations between formation rates and activation energies for ether formation with heats of adsorption of propyl acetate across Pt-zeolites and Pt-AlMCM41 suggest that dispersive interactions among the zeolite pore wall, surrounding molecules (e.g., propyl acetate), and transition states contribute to differences in performance among these catalysts. These effects appear responsible for Pt-FER providing the highest ether selectivities observed (∼50%), although the specific structural features responsible for this behavior remain uncertain and may reflect framework-specific confinement and transport effects. However, ether selectivities also appear sensitive to other zeolite properties, including channel dimensionality, which may influence diffusive transport between Pt and Brønsted acid sites. These findings illustrate that the topology of the aluminosilicate support impacts rates and selectivities for ester reduction by orders of magnitude: these differences reflect contributions of inter-function transport reminiscent of other bifunctional catalysts for hydrotreating reactions but also evidence from comparisons to titration calorimetry that the local solvation of reactive intermediates at Brønsted acid sites influences catalysis.

title: Single-cell-informed machine learning reveals prognostic and immune features of multiple myeloma
abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) is clinically heterogeneous, and the International Staging System (ISS) captures this heterogeneity only in part. We aimed to build a transcriptomic risk model anchored in single-cell and stage-associated gene expression, and to explore its immune context and therapeutic implications. Methods Bone marrow single-cell RNA sequencing data from 18 MM and 18 control samples were integrated with ISS stage-stratified RNA sequencing data from the MMRF CoMMpass cohort (n = 764).

title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
abstract: Nanofluidic memristors promise brain-inspired information processing with ions, yet their microscopic origin remains debated. So far, ionic memory has been attributed to ion-specific interactions, dynamic wetting, chemical reactions or mechanical deformations, yet typically without direct experimental evidence. Here, by combining operando interferometric imaging with electrokinetic measurements, we directly visualize voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels as the key origin of memristive hysteresis. We identify two distinct classes of blisters: unidirectional, driven by electrostatic forces on surface charges, and bidirectional, arising from osmotic pressure due to concentration polarization. This mechanistic framework explains device evolution and device-to-device variability, and reframes stochastic blistering as a functional design element. Our results constitute a direct proof of electromechanical coupling as a robust pathway to ionic memory in 2D nanochannels and open routes towards high-performance ionic memristors and electrically actuated nanofluidic valves.

title: Facet-Dependent Regulation of Reactive Oxygen Species Generation and Utilization Governs Biomass Oxidation
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are key intermediates in radical-mediated heterogeneous oxidation, yet the relationship between ROS generation and their effective utilization remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that crystal facets can differently influence ROS generation and utilization during biomass-derived alcohol/aldehyde oxidation. title: Electronic Control of Mechanistic Divergence in Iron-Catalyzed Olefin Carboamidation to β- and γ-Lactams
abstract: Regiodivergent synthetic strategies employing common precursors provide a powerful means of accessing structurally distinct molecular scaffolds. Herein, we report an electronically controlled, regiodivergent iron-catalyzed intramolecular olefin carboamidation of styrenyl dioxazolones that selectively affords either β- or γ-lactams using a range of carbon nucleophiles, including electron-rich arenes, allylsilanes, and propargylsilanes, thereby providing access to arylated, allylated, and allenylated products, respectively.

title: Unconventional SOC-activated Altermagnetic Spin Splitting and Half-Angle Locking of Spin Transport
abstract: Conventional altermagnetic spin splitting arises from staggered exchange and sublattice-dependent anisotropic hopping without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here we derive a low-energy effective model showing that SOC and staggered exchange can jointly activate additional spin splitting on momentum planes where the nonrelativistic contribution vanishes. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, this SOC-activated contribution produces d-wave spin splitting near $Γ$ with out-of-plane spin polarization. Its leading angular pattern counter-rotates by half the in-plane Néel-vector rotation angle. First-principles spin-transport calculations reveal a corresponding approximate half-angle locking between the Néel-vector orientation and the electric-field directions maximizing the signed longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Analytical transport calculations based on the effective model trace this locking to the same angular coupling between momentum and the Néel vector that governs the spin-splitting pattern. Our findings connect the microscopic mechanism of SOC-activated altermagnetic spin splitting to directional spin transport, providing a theoretical basis for probing Néel-vector orientation and controlling spin-current generation.
